second_rationale: Binding 'shall' duty; data governance practices (procedural) and quality standards for training/validation/testing data (substantive) serve system quality and testing, though a Risk Assessment reading (bias examination) is arguable; sanctions via Art 99.
Government request (not a legal requirement) that regulators publish updates on implementing the principles, aimed at public visibility; no compliance route attaches.

Council instruction to the Digital Policy Committee, binding within OECD internal procedure, to report on implementation (reporting) assigned to a committee (institutional); a follow-up/review mechanism rather than a compliance duty on AI actors; dimension could alternatively be Transparency or Enforcement.

Describes government's own approach of issuing principles non-statutorily for regulators to apply within remits; concerns implementation/enforcement architecture rather than imposing a duty (System-level only arguable).

Ministry guidelines without statutory force; imperative phrasing in a list of guidelines for industry is an expectation, not a legal duty; publication of transparency reports is a reporting measure with no enforcement route.

Recommendation to government to design proportionate, graded obligations across the value chain (institutional direction; content concerns substantive obligations); it frames a future regime rather than imposing a compliance duty.
'Should' assigns testing/evaluation and advisory functions to the AI Safety Institute; institution-building provision.
